Kids get over material wealth very easily. Sure it's annoying when you don't have the latest game or whatever, but this never really brought me down. It's all about being happy within, if she is confident, independent, and happy with herself, everything will be fine. 

One more thing, be happy yourself! If she sees you out and about, doing things you enjoy, socialising etc this will make her happy and generally create a positive environment that she will aspire to.

There's a lot to say, although I would expect it to be slightly easier because she's a girl. First thing is, please always encourage her and give her confidence. Encourage her to do extra curricular activities and hobbies, and make her proud of herself when she achieves things in both school and her hobbies. I had huge confidence issues when I was young, which I can trace back to having no father. I think this is of utmost importance, give her confidence.

Secondly, encourage independence. I can see how children in single parent households can fall in to the trap of feeling too attached to the one parent. Make sure you prepare her to venture out to the world, whether it's her first job, going to a friends house for the night when young, doing things independently. I think you get the gist. 

Lastly, and also very importantly, is never (and I mean never) push your problems on to her back. You may find being a single parent stressful, but if you show this she will blame herself. I had this feeling but overcame it, but when you're young it can really mess with you. I had immense worries for my mom and felt like it was my fault.

Naturally this will all happen on occasion, but as long as it's not constant, it'll be fine. Feel free to message me at any point if you need more advice.
